# 1.2.67 - the GM's browser rolls the dice

The twelfth and thirteenth stages on the way to 1.3.0, released together. The
first (E08) moves the Reroll to the GM: the GM's browser takes the Hope, throws
the dice again, takes the first result back and makes the action again, as one
step, from a record the GMs keep of every roll. The second (E28) has the
primary GM's browser throw the dice of every player's action and of every
statistic clicked on a sheet, and score each result from that roll rather than
from what the player's browser reports. The roller still sees the roll as their
own.

## Before installing

1. **Nothing in the world's data moves.** There is no migration step. Each
   player's browser forgets the Reroll bookmark it kept for itself until now,
   and the GMs' new records start empty, so a roll thrown before the update
   cannot be rerolled after it: the Reroll is refused and nothing is spent
   (read in the code, not measured).
2. **There is no setting for the new rolls.** The GM draws every player roll
   these notes name, always. The one exception is automatic: on a Daggerheart
   build that builds its rolls in a way this module was not written for, the
   players' rolls are thrown in their own browsers as before, and the GMs are
   told once for that version.

## At the table, as the GM

- **The primary GM's browser draws the players' rolls.** When a player presses
  Roll, the dice are thrown on the primary GM's browser, which writes the roll's
  message and keeps its record. Nobody is shown "the GM rolled": the roller's
  dice fall on their own screen in their own colours (or the dice sound plays
  without Dice So Nice), and a statistic rolled from the sheet is headed by the
  roller's character, never by the GM. The dice, the critical and the kind of
  roll (an action's or a reaction's) are the GM's; a draw not answered within
  30 seconds is not made and the player is told (a bound chosen, not measured
  at a table).
- **A roll that carried something you did not expect is flagged, not refused.**
  The statistic, the experiences, a bonus and advantage dice are still set in
  the player's roll window; one that differs from what the GM's browser
  expected, or a pick of yours that was never made, is whispered to the GMs and
  the roll stands. `game.drpg.rollFlags()` lists those of the last half hour.
- **With no GM connected an action waits**, and nothing is paid. Any other roll
  is still thrown, its card reads "Thrown with no GM connected - the GM will
  see it.", and it moves no Hope, Sanity or Despair.
- **The new card: Rolls made while no GM was connected.** When a GM connects,
  the primary GM gets one card listing each such roll with what it would have
  moved. **Grant all** gives each of them that - Hope, Daggerheart's Fear, the
  Monokuma's Despair - once; **Grant none** gives nothing. Either way each roll
  is decided and not asked again. An assistant GM's Grant all, like an
  assistant GM's Reroll, is made by the primary GM.
- **The Reroll is made by your browser.** A player asks for it; with no GM
  connected it is not made, and nothing is spent. A reload half way is put
  right when the primary GM's world loads, and a card says what happened:
  before the new dice counted, the first roll and the Hope come back; while the
  action was being made again, the card gives the character, the action and
  both totals - check what the action left (progress, items, traces, damage, a
  turn) and settle it by hand; while its Hope was being paid or given back, the
  first roll stands and the card asks you to check that character's Hope.
- **Taking a result back is the GM's.** A player's request to undo something
  is refused; the Reroll does it. Daggerheart's two rerolls are gone from a
  player's chat menu, and dice changed in a roll after it was thrown are put
  back by the primary GM's browser, and the GMs are told.
- **A player's private cards in an incident are posted by the primary GM's
  browser**, and their author names no player.
- **A player's transfer of an item to a party** (Daggerheart 2.10.6 and later)
  waits for the GM; the GM is told once a session.

## Changed

- **A roll is drawn for an action being taken** - paid for, or at its turn or
  stage - and once. An action is scored on its newest roll; a roll window's
  only cost is its experiences' Hope.
- **The Reroll settles what a fresh roll of those dice would**: Hope, Fear and
  a critical's second Hope only with Daggerheart's Hope and Fear automation on
  for players, Despair only with "Rolls grant Despair" on. A Reroll of a Work,
  a Sabotage or a Dynamic action is scored on what its first throw claimed.
  The card it replaced shows its total struck through and the old and the new
  total under its header.
- **What a Reroll takes back.** A clean-up's Reroll puts an erased trace back
  as it was; a Search's planted item survives its Reroll; a crisis action's
  keeps the critical's pick and the item used, and taking it back returns the
  item's healing and Hope; a Listen's hears what the roller could have heard.
  A trace a GM has written on, one somebody has found and one older than a
  Reroll can reach stay as they are, and the GMs are told which.
- **A Reroll that cannot be made is refused before anything is paid**: a
  clean-up or an Analyze whose first attempt can no longer be taken back, an
  Observe the GM is still describing, a roll gone from the chat or being put
  back, a second Reroll of a character while one is being made. If the GM's
  browser answers late, the player is told the Reroll may still be made.
- **Every resolution reads the GM's record of its roll**: Observe, Analyze, the
  hidden stash, a Palm, a theft from a stash, a trace's band, a project's
  progress, a Sabotage and its repair, the incident's opening and crisis
  actions, the clean-up and Stage 6. A roll that is not the player's, was thrown
  for another action, was already scored, is too old or did not earn the result
  is refused and the player told why. A crisis roll's statistic is the one the
  GM picked, whatever the window says.
- **Projects.** A Sabotage is made standing at its project, and a missed one
  tells the GMs its target, so its Reroll into a success freezes the project.
  A project's roll scores only on its own project. A Call's progress is added
  for the Call's price paid, once, in the project's room.
- **A Meddle's dice are thrown by the GM**, and a Meddle the GM refuses posts
  no dice.
- **A statistic rolled from the sheet** keeps its own card while an action's
  roll is under way, is a reaction even Shift-clicked, and stays readable to its
  roller after a reload. A Call armed while the roll window is open waits for
  the next roll, and the window says so. The reaction chip in an action's roll
  window no longer makes a drawn roll a reaction.
- **A direct murder the GM allows during an Eclipse is not announced to its
  killer before the lights**: the killer hears one answer, when the Eclipse
  ends.
- **What each browser holds.** The GMs' browsers keep four new records: each
  character's last roll for the Reroll, the clean-up attempts a Reroll may take
  back, the Reroll being made, and the players' drawn rolls. A player's browser
  keeps the ids of its own drawn rolls. Each player's action roll sends the
  GMs' browsers one more short message (two for a Search, a project, a Sabotage
  or a Dynamic action).

## Known gaps

- Grant all does not tick countdowns or Daggerheart's triggers.
- What a roll adds to its dice in the roll window is flagged, not refused, in
  this version.
- A Reroll that turns a Strike critical with no pick from its first throw asks
  the pick of the GM making the Reroll, not of the striker (untested).
- A roll thrown before the primary GM's browser loaded cannot be put back, only
  told; and the 3D dice of a changed roll may fall on every screen before it is
  put back (not measured).

## Checked

- The headless suite: 738 passed, 0 failed, 17 skipped, 0 red (631 at
  1.2.66). New in the suite: R215 to R219. The seventeen scenarios end green:
  11-killer-secrecy 14/14, its last red closed by this release, the security
  scenario 136/136, 40-flow 81/81, 15-held 16/16, 61-gmstore-case 93/93, and
  72-canary 84/87, its three reds each a later stage's or a Foundry limit. The
  suite takes about 22 minutes on the test machine.
- Daggerheart 2.10.8's GM-side handler runs in the headless harness, copied
  unchanged, and the harness now builds a roll the way Daggerheart does.
- An independent review in two rounds (security, and whether the change is
  correct and its tests measure); its findings were fixed in six commits after
  the first round and eight after the second.
- Not checked in a real Foundry yet: the Reroll and the drawn rolls at a table,
  with and without Dice So Nice, with two GMs, across a reload and on each
  Daggerheart build - the audit's live checks, section 9.2, items 89 to 105
  (LIVE-E08-01 to 05, LIVE-E28-01 to 12). The local release gate needs a local
  Foundry v14 and did not run for this release.
